core.title: Run the automated accessibility audit in every accessibility spec and assert on its violations
core.given: A browser-level spec (e2e test) is identified as an accessibility spec: it binds an accessibility test URN, or its own file name carries an accessibility name token (both identification signals per the profile)
core.when: The tester writes or changes that spec
core.then: The spec must run the stack's automated accessibility audit and assert on the reported violations in a way that can fail.
prefer: Assert that the audit reports no violations
Or use a bounded assertion: at most n violations
avoid: An accessibility spec that navigates the page but never runs the audit
Running the audit and then never asserting on the result
Tautological assertions that cannot fail, such as asserting the violation count is at least zero. These do not count as assertions
core.why: An accessibility spec that navigates but never runs the audit, or never asserts on the result, passes no matter what state the page is actually in.
evidence: The spec invokes the stack's automated accessibility audit (per the profile), under any local binding name
The audit's analysis runs, and its reported violations are asserted to be none, or at most a stated bound, in a way that can fail
The stack's accessibility-harness check reports no finding for the spec
verification: Identify accessibility specs only by the profile's accessibility test URN binding or accessibility name token (profile: urn.binding.test, suffix.a11y_test). The name token is matched against the file's own base name only: never a directory name, never inside a longer word, and task wording never counts.

Recognize browser-level specs per the profile (profile: roles.e2e_test.kinds), so a misnamed browser spec is still judged; a unit test that merely mentions a URN inside a string literal is not a browser spec. The browser-spec recognition is used together with the accessibility identification, never as a substitute for it.
Resolve the audit harness import under any local alias.

Accept assertions that can fail: asserting the reported violations are none, or at most a stated bound, using the stack's accepted assertion spellings (profile: idiom.test_constructs#a11y_assertions). Tautologies that cannot fail (for example asserting the count is at least zero) are not assertions and do not satisfy the rule.
Never scan the profile's excluded vendored and generated trees (profile: roots.excluded); this scopes the check only and is not a waiver.
Severity 3. Disposition: strict, as stated in the source; the source does not further define its enforcement semantics.

values: accessibility spec by file name: an accessibility name token in the file's own base name, bounded on the left by start-of-name or a separator and on the right by a separator or end-of-name, never inside a longer word and never a directory name (token patterns per the profile)
accessibility spec by URN: the spec binds an accessibility test URN (binding syntax per the profile)
browser-level spec (e2e test) per the profile's browser-spec definition, including misnamed spec files that carry a journey/test URN binding in header comments
accessibility-harness finding: the audit invocation is missing, or there is no assertion on the reported violations that can fail

fires: A newly written accessibility spec navigates to a page and asserts only on visible text, without running the accessibility audit
An accessibility spec binds the audit harness but never executes its analysis
An accessibility spec runs the audit but never asserts on the reported violations
An accessibility spec asserts the violation count with a tautology that cannot fail (for example, that it is at least zero)
A misnamed browser-level spec (recognized per the profile) that binds an accessibility test URN does not run the audit
doesNotFire: A browser-level spec that binds no accessibility test URN and has no accessibility name token in its own file name, even if the task mentions accessibility
A browser-level spec under a directory whose name alone carries the token, with no token in its own file name and no accessibility URN
A file whose base name contains the token only inside a longer word and has no accessibility URN
A unit test that only mentions an accessibility or journey URN inside a string literal
Files under the profile's excluded vendored and generated trees

profileRequirements.meaning: The name patterns that identify an accessibility spec among the stack's test files: an accessibility name token in the file's own base name.
profileRequirements.bunValue: **/a11y.*, **/a11y-*, **/a11y_*, **/*.a11y.*, **/*.a11y-*, **/*.a11y_*, **/*-a11y.*, **/*-a11y-*, **/*-a11y_*, **/*_a11y.*, **/*_a11y-*, **/*_a11y_* — an `a11y` token in the basename preceded by the start of the basename or one of `.`, `-`, `_` and followed by one of `.`, `-`, `_` or end-of-name (equivalent basename regex `(^|[._-])a11y([._-]|$)`); match the basename only, not directory names, and not `a11y` embedded in a longer word.

profileRequirements.meaning: The syntax by which a test file binds an accessibility test URN, so a spec with no name token is still identified as an accessibility spec.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the spec carries an `A11Y` test URN (needs a parser for test URNs in the file); a URN mentioned only inside a string literal is not a binding.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the browser-spec (e2e test) role: the population within which accessibility specs are identified, including misnamed ones.
profileRequirements.bunValue: browser_spec = a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// UserSystemFlow:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:user-system-flow:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged. A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser spec.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's automated accessibility audit harness: how a test invokes it and where the reported violations are exposed.
profileRequirements.bunValue: import `AxeBuilder` from `@axe-core/playwright` (under any local name) and call `new AxeBuilder(...).analyze()`; the audit result's `violations` carries the findings.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's accepted assertion spellings on the audit's reported violations (equal-to-none and bounded), and the tautological spelling that is rejected as not an assertion.
profileRequirements.bunValue: accepted equal-to-none: `toEqual([])`, `toHaveLength(0)`, `toBe(0)` (on the violations or its count); accepted bounded: `toBeLessThanOrEqual(n)`, `toBeLessThan(n)`; rejected tautology: `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)`.

profileRequirements.meaning: The one stack-wide list of vendored and generated trees that are never scanned.

bunOnly.text: `const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze(); expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);`

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral: an accessibility-identified browser-level spec must run the stack's automated accessibility audit and assert fail-capably on the reported violations. Everything concrete is stack data carried by the profile: the audit harness and its invocation (idiom.test_constructs#a11y_audit), the accepted and rejected assertion spellings (idiom.test_constructs#a11y_assertions, a map entry of the existing idiom.test_constructs key), the accessibility name-token patterns (suffix.a11y_test), the accessibility test-URN binding (urn.binding.test, an existing parametric key; bun.json gives no syntax beyond 'an A11Y test URN', so the bunValue carries that verbatim), the browser-spec population (roles.e2e_test.kinds) and the excluded trees (roots.excluded). The acceptance policy (none or a stated bound; tautologies are not assertions) stays in core verification and references the profile entry for the spellings. Only the detector/finding ids of this realization and the complete fix-hint code example remain bunOnly, per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys. Strict disposition and severity 3 are per-rule and kept in core verification, with no enforcement semantics added beyond the source's bare 'strict'.
